metadata.source: Visnu Prasada Sarma: Sāṃkhyakārikā: Māṭharācāryaviracita-"Māṭharavṛtti"-sahitā, Varanasi : The Chowkhamba Sanskrit Series Office 1970 (Chowkhamba Sanskrit Series, 296 [Work no. 56])

children.translated_text: Because of the affliction by the threefold suffering, inquiry arises into the cause that removes that affliction,
if in the seen (empirical means) it is thought purposeless, since there is no absolute and final cessation therein || 1 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭavad ānuśravikaḥ sa hy aviśuddhaḥ kṣayātiśayayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like the seen, what is based on <s>ānuśravika</s> (scriptural tradition) is indeed impure, marked by decay and excess,
its opposite is better, as it rests on discriminative knowledge of the manifest and the unmanifest || 2 ||
The root <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is unmodified; beginning with the <s>Mahad</s> (great principle) the seven are both <s>prakṛti</s> (source) and <s>vikṛti</s> (product),

children.text: ṣoḍaśakas tu vikāro na prakṛtir na vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: but the sixteen are products; and the <s>Puruṣa</s> (self) is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor <s>vikṛti</s> || 3 ||
Perception, inference, and the word of a trustworthy authority are accepted, since all means of knowledge are established (as such),

children.text: trividhaṃ pramāṇam iṣṭaṃ prameyasiddhiḥ pramāṇād dhi || 4 ||
children.translated_text: threefold knowledge-means are approved; for the establishment of the knowables is from the means of knowledge || 4 ||
Perception is a determinate apprehension with respect to its object; threefold inference is declared,
that (inference) being preceded by the mark and the marked; and the trustworthy hearing is indeed authoritative testimony || 5 ||

children.text: sāmānyatas tu dṛṣṭād atīndriyāṇāṃ pratītir anumānāt /
children.translated_text: From what is generally perceived, the apprehension of things beyond the senses is through inference,

children.text: tasmād api cāsiddhaṃ parokṣam āptāgamāt sādhyam || 6 ||
children.translated_text: and even that which is not (thus) established, being remote, is to be proved by the authoritative scripture of the trustworthy || 6 ||
Because of too great distance, because of proximity, because of injury to the senses, because of unsteadiness of mind,
because of subtlety, because of interposition, because of overpowering, and because of mingling with what is similar || 7 ||
Because of subtlety, the non-apprehension of that is not due to non-existence; its apprehension is from its effect,

children.text: mahadādi tac ca kāryaṃ prakṛtivirūpaṃ sarūpaṃ ca || 8 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Mahad</s> and what follows are that effect; and it is both unlike and like to <s>Prakṛti</s> || 8 ||
Because the non-existent does not produce, because of the taking up of material cause, because of the absence of everything’s arising from everything,

children.text: śaktasya śakyakaraṇāt kāraṇabhāvāc ca sat kāryam || 9 ||
children.translated_text: because the capable produces what can be produced, and because of the state of cause, the effect exists (pre-exists) || 9 ||

children.text: hetumad anityam avyāpi sakriyam anekam āśritaṃ liṅgam /
children.translated_text: The sign (mark) is accompanied by a cause, impermanent, non-pervasive, active, manifold, dependent,
composite, relative to another; the manifest is such; the unmanifest is the opposite || 10 ||

children.text: triguṇam aviveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyam acetana prasavadharmi /
children.translated_text: The manifest is three-<s>guṇa</s> (constituted of three qualities), non-discriminating, an object, general, non-conscious, possessing the nature of production,

children.text: vyaktaṃ tathā pradhānaṃ tadviparītas tathā ca pumān || 11 ||
children.translated_text: so also is the <s>Pradhāna</s> (<s>Prakṛti</s> as the chief cause); and the opposite of that is likewise the <s>Pumān</s> (<s>Puruṣa</s>) || 11 ||
The <s>guṇa</s>s have the activities of mutual overpowering, support, generation, and pairing with one another,
their natures being pleasure, pain, and delusion, and their purposes being illumination, activity, and restraint || 12 ||

children.text: sattvaṃ laghu prakāśakam iṣṭam upaṣṭambhakaṃ calaṃ ca rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is light, illuminating, and desirable; <s>Rajas</s> is mobile and supports (the others);

children.text: guru varaṇakam eva tamaḥ pradīpavac cārthato vṛttiḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tamas</s> is heavy and veiling; and function is according to the object, like a lamp || 13 ||
The unmanifest is established because of the tri-<s>guṇa</s> nature, because of the absence of the reversal of that,
and because the effect is of the nature of the cause’s qualities; thus even the unmanifest is established || 14 ||

children.text: bhedānāṃ parimāṇāt samanvayāc chaktitaḥ pravṛtteś ca /
children.translated_text: From the limitedness of differences, from the convergence (coherence), from the fact of activity according to power,
from the division of cause and effect, and from the non-division (continuity) of the universal form || 15 ||

children.text: kāraṇam asty avyaktaṃ pravartate triguṇataḥ samudayāc ca /
children.translated_text: The unmanifest cause exists; it operates because of the three <s>guṇa</s>s and because of their aggregation,
because of transformation, like water, and because of particularity according to the substratum of each <s>guṇa</s> in turn || 16 ||
Because a composite is for the sake of another, because of the inversion (contrast) with the three <s>guṇa</s>s, and because of a governing basis,
<s>Puruṣa</s> exists, because of being an enjoyer, and because of activity aimed at isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) || 17 ||
From the regulation of birth, death, and instruments (organs), and because they do not operate simultaneously,
the multiplicity of <s>Puruṣa</s> is established, and also because of the contrariety to the tri-<s>guṇa</s> || 18 ||

children.text: tasmāc ca viparyāsāt siddhaṃ sākṣitvam asya puruṣasya /
children.translated_text: And from that contrariety, the witnesshood of this <s>Puruṣa</s> is established,
isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>), neutrality, seership, and the state of non-agency || 19 ||

children.text: tasmāt tatsaṃyogād acetanaṃ cetanāvad iva liṅgam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the conjunction with that (Puruṣa), the non-conscious mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>, subtle body) appears as if conscious,
and though the <s>guṇa</s>s are the agents, thus he (Puruṣa), being indifferent, seems as if the doer || 20 ||
For the sake of the vision of the <s>Puruṣa</s>, and for the sake of isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) of <s>Pradhāna</s>,

children.text: paṅgvandhavad ubhayor api saṃyogas tatkṛtaḥ sargaḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: the conjunction of both, like the lame and the blind, occurs; from that is produced creation || 21 ||

children.text: prakṛter mahāṃs tato 'haṅkāras tasmād gaṇaś ca ṣoḍaśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: From <s>Prakṛti</s> comes the <s>Mahān</s> (Great Principle); from that the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle); from that the group of sixteen,

children.text: tasmād api ṣoḍaśakāt pañcabhyaḥ pañca bhūtāni || 22 ||
children.translated_text: and from this very sixteen, from the five, the five elements arise || 22 ||

children.text: adhyavasāyo buddhir dharmo jñānaṃ virāga aiśvaryam /
children.translated_text: Determination is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect); virtue, knowledge, dispassion, and lordliness are (its) forms when <s>sāttvika</s>,

children.text: sāttvikam etad rūpaṃ tāmasam asmād viparyastam || 23 ||
children.translated_text: the opposite of these from it is <s>tāmasa</s> (their perversion) || 23 ||
Self-appropriation is <s>ahaṅkāra</s>; from that twofold creation proceeds,
the elevenfold of the senses, and the pentad of subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>) || 24 ||
The elevenfold, being <s>sāttvika</s>, proceeds from the modified <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (<s>vaikṛta</s>),

children.text: bhūtādes tanmātraḥ sa tāmasas taijasād ubhayam || 25 ||
children.translated_text: the subtle element from the <s>bhūta</s>-type (elemental) is <s>tāmasa</s>; from the <s>taijasa</s> (rajasic) are both || 25 ||
The knowledge-senses (<s>buddhīndriya</s>) are those called ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose,
speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are said to be the action-senses (<s>karmendriya</s>) || 26 ||

children.text: ubhayātmakam atra manaḥ saṅkalpakam indriyaṃ ca sādharmyāt /
children.translated_text: Here the mind (<s>manas</s>) is of a dual nature, being both deliberative (saṅkalpaka) and, by similarity, an organ (indriya),
manifoldness (of the senses) is due to the specific transformations of the <s>guṇa</s>s, and also because of the diversity of what is to be apprehended || 27 ||
For the five (knowledge-senses), with respect to forms and the rest (rūpa, etc.), the function is held to be mere illumination (āloka) alone,
but for the five (action-senses) the functions are speech, taking, moving about (enjoyment), evacuation, and procreation (delight) || 28 ||

children.text: svālakṣaṇyā vṛttis trayasya saiṣā bhavaty asāmānyā /
children.translated_text: By their own particular marks (svālakṣaṇa), the function of the three (inner organs) is this distinctive (asāmānya) one,
whereas the function of the general organs (i.e., the senses as common instruments) is (carried by) the five breaths, beginning with <s>Prāṇa</s>; these are the five winds || 29 ||

children.text: yugapac catuṣṭayasya hi vṛttiḥ kramaśaś ca tasya nirdiṣṭā /
children.translated_text: And the function of the fourfold set (of inner organs together with vital winds) occurs simultaneously, and also for that (set) a sequential operation is stated,

children.text: dṛṣṭe tathāpy adṛṣṭe trayasya tatpūrvikā vṛttiḥ || 30 ||
children.translated_text: similarly in the seen and in the unseen; for the three (inner organs) the function is preceded by that (viz., by the operation of the senses) || 30 ||
Each takes up its own respective function, whose cause is one another’s prompting (mutual instigation),

children.text: puruṣārtha eva hetur na kenacit kāryate karaṇam || 31 ||
children.translated_text: only the purpose of the <s>Puruṣa</s> is the cause; no instrument does anything by (its own) agency || 31 ||
The instrument (karaṇa) is of thirteen kinds; it effects taking in, holding, and illumination,

children.text: kāryaṃ ca tasya daśadhāhāryaṃ dhāryaṃ prakāśyaṃ ca || 32 ||
children.translated_text: and its product (kārya) is tenfold: what is to be taken in, to be held, and to be illuminated || 32 ||

children.text: antaḥkaraṇaṃ trividhaṃ daśadhā bāhyaṃ trayasya viṣayākhyam /
children.translated_text: The inner instrument is threefold; the outer is tenfold, named the objects of the three (sets of senses),
the external instrument operates in the present time, the internal instrument operates across the three times (past, present, future) || 33 ||
Of these, the five knowledge-senses have as their objects the particular and the non-particular (the specific and the generic),

children.text: vāg bhavati śabdaviṣayā śeṣāny api pañcaviṣayāṇi || 34 ||
children.translated_text: speech has sound as its object; the remaining (action-senses) too have five (kinds of) objects || 34 ||

children.text: sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhiḥ sarvaṃ viṣayam avagāhate yasmāt /
children.translated_text: Because the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), along with the inner instrument, apprehends every object,

children.text: tasmāt trividhaṃ karaṇaṃ dvāri dvārāṇi śeṣāṇi || 35 ||
children.translated_text: therefore the instrument is threefold (within), while the others are the doors; at the doorway (they stand) || 35 ||
These specific modes of the <s>guṇa</s>s, distinct from one another, are like lamps,
having illuminated the entire purpose of the <s>Puruṣa</s>, they deliver it to the intellect || 36 ||

children.text: sarvaṃ pratyupabhogaṃ yasmāt puruṣasya sādhayati buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the intellect accomplishes for the <s>Puruṣa</s> all experiential enjoyment,

children.text: saiva ca viśinaṣṭi tataḥ pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ sūkṣmam || 37 ||
children.translated_text: that very intellect discriminates thereafter the subtle difference between <s>Pradhāna</s> (<s>Prakṛti</s>) and <s>Puruṣa</s> || 37 ||

children.text: tanmātrāṇy aviśeṣās tebhyo bhūtāni pañca pañcabhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>) are the non-particulars; from these arise the five gross elements (<s>bhūta</s>),

children.text: ete smṛtā viśeṣāḥ śāntā ghorāś ca mūḍhāś ca || 38 ||
children.translated_text: these are remembered as the particulars (viśeṣa), and they are serene, terrible, and dull (threefold) || 38 ||

children.text: sūkṣmā mātāpitṛjāḥ saha prabhūtais tridhā viśeṣāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: The particulars are threefold: subtle (innate), born of mother and father, and together with the powerful (supernormal) ones,
of these, the subtle are fixed; those born of mother and father cease (at death) || 39 ||
The subtle mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>), produced earlier, unattached, determinate, extending from the <s>Mahad</s> down to the subtlest,
wanders, devoid of enjoyment, perfumed by dispositions (bhāva), through transmigration || 40 ||

children.text: citraṃ yathāśrayamṛte sthāṇvādibhyo vinā yathā chāyā /
children.translated_text: Variegated (experience), apart from its support, exists no more than shade without a post or the like,

children.text: tadvad vināviśeṣais tiṣṭhati na nirāśrayaṃ liṅgam || 41 ||
children.translated_text: so too, without the particulars, the <s>liṅga</s> does not remain unsupported || 41 ||
This (liṅga) is for the sake of the <s>Puruṣa</s>’s purpose, and through the connection of occasional cause and occasioned,
because of the pervasiveness-capacity of <s>Prakṛti</s>, it stands forth like an actor || 42 ||

children.text: sāṃsiddhikāś ca bhāvāḥ prākṛtikā vaikṛtāś ca dharmādyāḥ /
children.translated_text: And innate attainments (sāṃsiddhika) and natural, as well as modified, qualities such as virtue and the rest,
are observed resting on the instruments, and the effects such as embryo and the rest rest on (material) products || 43 ||

children.text: dharmeṇa gamanam ūrdhvaṃ gamanam adhastād bhavaty adharmeṇa /
children.translated_text: By virtue (dharma) there is upward going; by vice (adharma) there is downward going,
by knowledge there is release (<s>apavarga</s>), and bondage is held to be through error (viparyaya) || 44 ||

children.text: vairāgyāt prakṛtilayaḥ saṃsāro rājasād bhavati rāgāt /
children.translated_text: By dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) there is dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s>; samsara arises from <s>Rajas</s> through passion (rāga),
by lordly power (<s>aiśvarya</s>) there is unobstructedness, and through its contrary there is the opposite of that || 45 ||
This is the projection of cognitions (pratyaya-sarga), named error, incapacity, satisfaction, and success,
through the mutual clash of inequality of the <s>guṇa</s>s; and its divisions are fifty || 46 ||

children.text: pañca viparyayabhedā bhavanty aśakteś ca karaṇavaikalyāt /
children.translated_text: The five are divisions of error, and of incapacity because of the defectiveness of the instruments,
satisfaction has twenty-eight divisions, and success is eightfold || 47 ||

children.text: bhedas tamaso 'ṣṭavidho mohasya ca daśavidho mahāmohaḥ /
children.translated_text: Error (tamas) has eight divisions, delusion (moha) ten, and great delusion (mahāmoha),
<s>Tāmisra</s> is eighteenfold, and likewise is <s>Andhatāmisra</s> || 48 ||
The incapacity is stated as the impairments of the eleven senses together with impairments of the intellect,
there are seventeen impairments of the intellect; satisfaction and success arise from error’s (removal/contrary) || 49 ||
And the four internal satisfactions are called nature (prakṛti), material cause (upādāna), time, and fortune,

children.text: bāhyā viṣayoparamāt pañca nava ca tuṣṭayo 'bhihitāḥ || 50 ||
children.translated_text: the external satisfactions are said to be nine, five from the cessation of objects and (in all) nine || 50 ||
Conjecture (ūha), authoritative word (śabda), study (adhyayana), the triple removal of suffering, obtaining a friend,

children.text: dānaṃ ca siddhayo 'ṣṭau siddheḥ pūrvo 'ṅkuśas trividhaḥ || 51 ||
children.translated_text: and giving (dāna) are the eight successes; prior to success is a threefold goad (spur) of success || 51 ||

children.text: na vinā bhāvair liṅgaṃ na vinā liṅgena bhāvanirvṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Without dispositions (<s>bhāva</s>), the subtle mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>) does not (come to) be, and without the subtle mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>) there is no accomplishment (occurrence) of dispositions (<s>bhāva</s>),

children.text: liṅgākhyo bhāvākhyas tasmād bhavati dvidhā sargaḥ || 52 ||
children.translated_text: therefore the projection (creation) is twofold, called subtle mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>-named) and disposition (<s>bhāva</s>-named) || 52 ||

children.text: aṣṭavikalpo daivas tairyagyonaś ca pañcadhā bhavati /
children.translated_text: The divine (birth) is eightfold in its varieties, and the animal womb is fivefold,
and the human is of a single kind; thus in summary the material (elemental) projection (<s>sarga</s>) is stated || 53 ||

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ sattvaviśālas tamoviśālaś ca mūlataḥ sargaḥ /
children.translated_text: Upwards there is an abundance of <s>Sattva</s>, and at the root (below) an abundance of <s>Tamas</s> is the projection,
in the middle, an abundance of <s>Rajas</s>, extending from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a pillar (a mere clod or plant) || 54 ||

children.text: atra jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnoti cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here the conscious <s>Puruṣa</s> obtains suffering caused by old age and death,
therefore, because of the non-cessation of the subtle mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>), suffering (is to be explained) in summary || 55 ||
Thus this undertaking, produced by <s>Prakṛti</s>, extends from the Great (<s>Mahad</s>) down to the elements as its domain,
for the sake of the release of each <s>Puruṣa</s>, an undertaking whose end is for another, as if (it were) for its own sake || 56 ||
Just as milk, being unintelligent, proceeds for the sake of the growth of the calf,
so does <s>Pradhāna</s> (<s>Prakṛti</s>) proceed for the sake of the release of the <s>Puruṣa</s> || 57 ||
Just as people engage in actions for the sake of the cessation of eagerness (curiosity, anxious expectancy),
so too the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) engages for the sake of the release of the <s>Puruṣa</s> || 58 ||

children.text: raṅgasya darśayitvā nivartate nartakī yathā nṛtyāt /
children.translated_text: Just as a dancing girl, having shown the performance of the stage, withdraws from the dance,
so <s>Prakṛti</s>, having made herself manifest to the <s>Puruṣa</s>, withdraws || 59 ||
By manifold means, being helpful to the non-helping (non-agent) man (<s>puṃs</s>, i.e., <s>Puruṣa</s>),

children.text: guṇavaty aguṇasya satas tasyārtham apārthakaṃ carati || 60 ||
children.translated_text: being possessed of <s>guṇa</s>s for the sake of one without <s>guṇa</s>s, being existent for the sake of one that is (merely) existent, she (Prakṛti) acts for his sake, though that (sake) is purposeless (to herself) || 60 ||

children.text: prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ na kiñcid astīti me matir bhavati /
children.translated_text: My view is this: nothing is more delicate (subtle and considerate) than <s>Prakṛti</s>,

children.text: yā dṛṣṭāsmīti punar na darśanam upaiti puruṣasya || 61 ||
children.translated_text: who, once seen as ‘I have been seen,’ does not again come to the sight of the <s>Puruṣa</s> || 61 ||

children.text: tasmān na badhyate nāpi mucyate nāpi saṃsarati kaścit /
children.translated_text: Therefore no one is bound, nor is anyone released, nor does anyone transmigrate,

children.text: saṃsarati badhyate mucyate ca nānāśrayā prakṛtiḥ || 62 ||
children.translated_text: it is <s>Prakṛti</s], resting on various supports, that transmigrates, is bound, and is released || 62 ||

children.text: rūpaiḥ saptabhir evaṃ badhnāty ātmānam ātmanā prakṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: With seven forms, in this way, <s>Prakṛti</s> binds herself by herself,

children.text: saiva ca puruṣasyārthaṃ prati vimocayaty ekarūpeṇa || 63 ||
children.translated_text: and that very (Prakṛti), with a single form, effects release for the sake of the <s>Puruṣa</s> || 63 ||

children.text: evaṃ tattvābhyāsān nāsmi na me nāham ity apariśeṣam /
children.translated_text: Thus, from practice regarding the principles (tattva-abhyāsa), ‘I am not,’ ‘this is not mine,’ ‘I am not this’—completely,
through non-misperception there arises knowledge that is pure and solitary || 64 ||

By that (knowledge) the <s>Puruṣa</s>, being established as a spectator, at ease (in himself), sees <s>Prakṛti</s>, whose production has ceased, who, because of the purpose being accomplished, has ceased from (her) seven forms,

children.text: prakṛtiṃ paśyati puruṣaḥ prekṣakavad avasthitaḥ svasthaḥ || 65 ||
children.translated_text: like a spectator (he views her), remaining self-possessed || 65 ||
Through the attainment of right knowledge, when virtue and the rest (dharma, etc.) no longer obtain as causes,
he remains, by the force of residual impressions, with body sustained, like the whirling of a wheel || 67 ||
When the body breaks up, since his purpose has been accomplished and <s>Pradhāna</s> has ceased,
he attains isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) that is absolute and ultimate—both indeed || 68 ||
This knowledge of the <s>Puruṣa</s>’s purpose, profound (esoteric), was taught by the supreme seer,
where the abiding, arising, and dissolution of beings are contemplated || 69 ||

children.text: etat pavitryam agryaṃ munir āsuraye 'nukampayā pradadau /
children.translated_text: The sage gave this foremost purifier, out of compassion, to <s>Āsuri</s>,

children.text: āsurir api pañcaśikhāya tena ca bahulīkṛtaṃ tantram || 70 ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Āsuri</s> to <s>Pañcaśikha</s>; and by him the system (tantra) was made abundant (widely promulgated) || 70 ||
Received through a succession of disciples, this (teaching) was also abbreviated by <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s> for the noble-minded,
having rightly understood the established doctrine (siddhānta) || 71 ||

children.text: saptatyāṃ kila yo 'rthās te 'rthāḥ kṛtsnasya ṣaṣṭitantrasya /
children.translated_text: The topics that are in the Seventy (verses) are indeed the topics of the entire sixty-tantra (i.e., the whole tradition),
devoid of anecdotes and free from refutations of others’ views || 72 ||

children.text: tasmāt samāsadṛṣṭaṃ śāstram idaṃ nārthataś ca parihīnam /
children.translated_text: Therefore this scripture, seen in compendium, is not deficient in meaning,

children.text: tantrasya ca bṛhanmūrter darpaṇasaṅkrāntam iva bimbam || 73 ||
children.translated_text: and it is like a reflection transferred from the larger form of the treatise, as in a mirror || 73 ||
